subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core session PIN gate, and what trusted secret source, verifier path, session state, reset behavior, and default mode should define that boundary?
rationale: The request touches core auth config, secret handling, prompt-injection resistance, tool execution blocking, and session lifecycle semantics; automation cannot safely choose those security defaults.

options.title: Sponsor Core Opt-In Design
options.body: Define an opt-in core session-auth design with SecretRef-compatible storage, a trusted TypeScript verifier, reset semantics, and tests before coding.

options.title: Route To Plugin Contract
options.body: Keep core unchanged for now and ask for a plugin or generic guardrail API proposal if existing hooks are insufficient.

options.title: Decline Core PIN Gate
options.body: Close the direction as out of scope if maintainers do not want session-level PIN authentication in core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Core Opt-In Design
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in core session-auth design with SecretRef-compatible storage, a trusted TypeScript verifier, reset semantics, and tests before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security/auth boundary decision and @steipete has adjacent auth-session history plus CODEOWNERS/security context in the inspected files.
